title: Examining AI Use in Educational Contexts: A Scoping Meta-Review and Bibliometric Analysis
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the broad question of how artificial intelligence has been studied across educational contexts, and what can be learned from the existing body of systematic reviews. The authors note that AI in education research has expanded rapidly, but prior work had not sufficiently synthesized the findings of those reviews to identify overall trends, common findings, and gaps. To address this, they conducted a scoping meta-review and bibliometric analysis of 126 systematic reviews published from 2014 through mid-August 2023.

The paper is not an intervention study of a single AI tool; rather, it synthesizes evidence on AI applications such as machine learning, intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, chatbots, adaptive learning, and automated assessment across PreK-12 and higher education. The included reviews span multiple subjects, including mathematics, and multiple settings, though many reviews did not report detailed contextual information. The analysis combines keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship, geographic distribution, and thematic synthesis to map the field.

Main conclusions are that machine learning is the most frequently studied AI type, followed by intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, and data mining. The review identifies three major themes: AI’s impact on student learning, teaching, and administrative/institutional services. Across educational levels, AI is most often associated with adaptive/personalized learning, assessment, and data-driven support, but the literature is much richer in higher education than in PreK-12, and especially limited in reporting contextual details, learner characteristics, and implementation specifics. The authors argue that future research should provide more granular evidence, stronger teacher preparation, and clearer distinctions between AI for education and AI literacy education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed scoping meta-review and bibliometric analysis, which is methodologically systematic but does not estimate primary causal effects. It synthesizes review findings rather than primary studies, so it provides useful mapping evidence but not high-credibility impact estimation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper offers useful adjacent evidence for likely AI effects in education, especially around adaptive learning, ITS, and administration, but it reports no pooled effect sizes and no direct middle school math intervention outcomes. Its impact on the target question is therefore informative but indirect and modest.

interventions.use_case: Scoping meta-review and bibliometric synthesis of AI use in education across 126 systematic reviews, including intelligent tutoring systems, machine learning, learning analytics, chatbots, adaptive learning, and related educational AI applications.

finding.finding_summary: This is a tertiary scoping meta-review rather than a primary impact study, so it does not estimate a pooled effect of AI on student outcomes. It synthesizes 126 systematic reviews and finds broad but uneven evidence of AI’s influence on teaching, learning, and administration, with stronger concentration in higher education than PreK-12 and notable evidence gaps in contextual reporting and quality assessment.
finding.measure: Systematic review synthesis; bibliometric indicators; thematic coding of review findings

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature, AI was frequently associated with administrative efficiency gains such as automation of repetitive tasks, data analysis, decision support, and chatbot-based support services. The paper summarizes prior reviews indicating AI can streamline grading, student inquiries, resource allocation, and institutional operations, but it does not report a pooled quantitative effect size.
finding.measure: Administrative efficiency and service functions reported in systematic reviews
finding.study_size: n=126 reviews (synthesis); specific underlying review sizes vary

finding.finding_summary: The review identifies mathematics as one of the more common subject areas in AI education reviews and highlights adaptive systems and personalization in mathematics education as a recurring theme. It cites prior review evidence that AI can tailor guidance by proficiency level and learning behaviors, but does not provide a pooled estimate or direct middle school math outcome.
finding.measure: Mathematics education themes and reported AI use in math learning/teaching reviews

finding.finding_summary: The paper notes intelligent tutoring systems as one of the most studied AI applications and links them to personalized support, active learning, and improved learning performance. However, this is a synthesis of review-level claims rather than a direct causal estimate, so no effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Mathematics/learning performance as reported in prior reviews of ITS and AI tutoring
